extracted.intended_audience: ML conference organizers, program chairs, reviewers, and ML researchers interested in submitting or adjudicating refutations/critiques
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, evaluating, and reviewing submissions to a dedicated 'Refutations & Critiques' (R&C) track at major machine-learning conferences; covers submission standards, review principles, and track governance to ensure robust post-publication correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct, Rigorous and Meticulous
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must demonstrate methodological soundness. Critiques involving experiments should ensure reproducibility and transparent analysis; theoretical arguments must be logically coherent. All claims require strong, verifiable evidence (e.g., experimental results, proofs, data re-analysis) allowing for independent assessment by the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim guidance: 'Submissions must demonstrate methodological soundness. Critiques involving experiments should ensure reproducibility and transparent analysis; theoretical arguments must be logically coherent. All claims require strong, verifiable evidence (e.g., experimental results, proofs, data re-analysis) allowing for independent assessment by the reviewers.' Practical implications: provide code/data, clear experimental protocols, and verifiable analysis; ensure proofs have no hidden assumptions. Example anti-pattern: hand-wavy counterclaims without reproducible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must address substantive aspects of the original work, such as its central claims, core methodologies, or foundational assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim: 'The critique should have meaningful implications, clearly articulating why the identified issues (e.g., unsupported conclusions, flawed assumptions or results, limited applicability of results) are important to the broader research community.' Reject submissions that 'solely challenge attribution errors or nitpick minor details.' Focus on issues that materially affect interpretation or use of the original paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must aim to correct and improve the scientific record and positively guide future research, rather than being solely dismissive or adversarial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim: 'Submissions should articulate their contribution to collective understanding, potentially offering corrections, alternative interpretations, or suggestions for better practices, all while maintaining a professional tone. Submissions must focus on the research and not on the people who conducted it.' Practical expectations: suggest remedies, alternative analyses, clearer framing, or mitigations; avoid ad hominem language and sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be judged based on how influential the criticized work is and how significantly the submissions change the field’s understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim: 'Responses or critiques that substantially shift widespread, deeply held important beliefs represent the most consequential forms of scientific correction, and the R&C track should recognize and reward such contributions.' Implication: prioritize critiques that affect major lines of work, benchmarks, or commonly used methodologies rather than marginal counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link Accepted Papers to Prior Work (Explicit Linking / Errata-style)
rubrics_metrics.description: A response or a critique is more than a citation; it should be explicitly linked to the publication being critiqued, similar to how corrigenda and errata are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: accepted R&C papers should be associated with the original paper in conference listings/archives (e.g., hyperlinked, flagged as a critique/erratum). The paper cites NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks track as an example of explicit linking. This increases discoverability and frames R&C contributions as part of the scientific record rather than standalone commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bespoke Reviewing Standards for R&C Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Review criteria for R&C submissions should be tailored and distinct from regular research-paper criteria, reflecting unique aspects of critique work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim example checks: 'whether the criticized paper’s authors are aware of the objections and have been given proper opportunity to respond' and 'double-blind review may not be realistic (e.g., if public interactions such as GitHub issues are referenced for evidence).' Practical elements: accept references to public discussions as evidence, permit reviewer assignment that accounts for conflicts, and include domain experts who can adjudicate correctness of the critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Response / Participation Mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of the original work should likely be invited to participate in a unique capacity to ensure fairness and accuracy of the critique process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested practice: provide an author-response or comment/response phase analogous to journal comment/response systems; allow original authors to clarify, correct, or refute claims prior to final decision. This helps reduce wrongful discrediting and promotes constructive scientific exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous Review Standards and Multiple Rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Refutations themselves must be held to high standards—rigorous review, and potentially multiple rounds of author-reviewer interaction, are necessary to avoid promulgating flawed critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim concern: 'R&C Track Papers Might Themselves Be Misleading, Incorrect, Flawed or Fraudulent.' Mitigation: require multiple reviewing iterations, allow back-and-forth between critique authors and original authors (or reviewers), and ensure reviewers have appropriate expertise. Use SAC/AC oversight to prevent one-sided decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Beyond Reproducibility (Broader Purview)
rubrics_metrics.description: The track should accept submissions that go beyond mere reproducibility checks, including critiques of assumptions, misleading narratives, incorrect analyses, or erroneous conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim: 'While reproducibility assessments are welcome as submissions, this R&C Track aims to construct a broader aegis to explicitly encourage submissions that seek to rectify the field.' Examples: papers showing a result is technically reproducible but misinterpreted, or demonstrating that key assumptions are unrealistic and therefore conclusions do not generalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and Verifiability of the Critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Critiques should be transparent about methods, data, and code so that reviewers and the community can independently verify the claims made by the refutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical expectations: release code, seeds, datasets or clear instructions; include re-analysis artifacts and provenance where possible. This overlaps with 'Correct, Rigorous and Meticulous' but is emphasized repeatedly: evidence must be 'strong, verifiable' and allow independent assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardrails Against Frivolous or Adversarial Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Track design and review criteria should actively mitigate risks of frivolous, adversarial, or unconstructive submissions and coordinated criticism campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim concern and mitigation: 'The guiding principles ... demanding that submissions be “Rigorous and Meticulous,” “Substantive,” “Significant” and “Constructive” - are specifically intended to mitigate these risks.' Operational measures: strict desk-reject standards for nitpicking/attribution-only complaints, conflict-of-interest handling, requirement of substantive evidence, and enforcing professional tone; consider sanctions or filtering for abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with Conference Structures and Pilot Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The R&C Track should be integrated with existing conference timelines and review processes and should start with a pilot to evaluate effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim: 'This track would naturally be integrated with existing conference structures, including timelines and review processes, and would likely include a pilot to evaluate whether the proposed track is effective.' Practical implications: align submission deadlines, reviewing cadence, and publication format with the main conference to ensure visibility and operational feasibility; run a pilot to measure uptake, quality, and impact before full rollout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host at Prestigious Conferences to Confer Legitimacy and Visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosting the R&C Track at major ML conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR) confers legitimacy, visibility, and archival permanence to refutation work, increasing its impact and discoverability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim rationale: 'The considerable prestige of NeurIPS can legitimize R&C research as an essential scientific contribution.' Practical outcome: R&C publications become citable, visible, and more likely to be linked to original papers, helping correct the scientific record more effectively than blog posts or social media.
